author: Yaqeen Advisory
title: Audit readiness: a checklist to complete before your auditor arrives
summary: Most audit delays come from missing schedules and slow responses to requests. This checklist helps you prepare before fieldwork starts.
metaTitle: Audit Readiness Checklist: Prepare Before Fieldwork
metaDescription: An audit readiness checklist: closing schedules, reconciliations, working papers, related-party disclosures and a tracker for the auditor’s requests.
body:
Audits are quicker, cheaper and calmer when the evidence is ready before the auditor asks for it. This checklist covers what to prepare. Statutory audit is carried out by an independent auditor appointed by you; the checklist is about your side of the work.

## Before fieldwork

1. **Close the books properly.** All months reconciled and reviewed, accruals and provisions posted, depreciation run.
2. **Prepare closing schedules.** Fixed assets, receivables and payables ageing, loans, taxes payable, provisions and prepaid items, each agreeing to the trial balance.
3. **Reconcile bank and loan balances.** Obtain confirmations or statements as at year-end.
4. **Review related-party transactions.** List parties, transactions and balances, and check the disclosures.
5. **Assemble supporting documents.** Contracts, invoices, board approvals and tax filings, filed by schedule.
6. **Review key balances for reasonableness.** Look for unusual movements and be ready to explain them.

## During the audit

- Keep one tracker of the auditor's requests, with an owner and a due date for each.
- Respond in batches, with supporting documents attached.
- Agree a single point of contact on both sides.

## After the audit

- Record the findings and fix the causes, not just the symptoms.
- Update your month-end checklist so next year starts from a better base.

## Start early

Starting one to two months before fieldwork gives time to fix issues. If your records need more work, a books clean-up before the audit is usually cheaper than fixing problems during it.
